pains.title: One combined report hides which clinic makes money
pains.problem: Each clinic has its own rent, staff and ramp up. In one report, a busy older clinic can cover a weak new one for years.
pains.how: Lucid tags every transaction to a clinic, shares common costs by a consistent rule and sends a monthly profit and loss per clinic. Separate entities are reconciled into a combined view.

pains.title: Reimbursement per visit falls while costs rise
pains.problem: Payers set the rate and independent clinics have little leverage, while wages and rent keep climbing.
pains.how: Lucid reports revenue by payer and by clinic, and CFO scenarios test a rate cut or wage increase first. Lucid does not negotiate with payers or code visits.

pains.title: Unpaid visits and cash that arrives late
pains.problem: Insurance pays weeks after the visit, but payroll and rent are due now. Visit caps and authorizations can leave care unpaid.
pains.how: Your biller keeps claims and authorizations. Lucid reconciles deposits to the bank and forecasts cash so payroll weeks at risk show early.

faq_title: Physical therapy accounting questions owners ask

faq.q: How do I know which of my physical therapy clinics is actually making money?
faq.a: You need a profit and loss for each location, not one combined report. Lucid sets up your books so every dollar is tagged to a clinic, shares common costs by a consistent rule, and sends a monthly report per location before you decide to open the next one.

faq.q: Why is there never enough cash in my physical therapy practice even when we are busy?
faq.a: Insurance pays weeks after the visit, but payroll and rent are due now, so growth can drain cash. Lucid reconciles your deposits to the bank, tracks payer mix, and forecasts cash so you see a gap before it arrives.

faq.q: How can I tell what denials and visit limits cost my practice?
faq.a: It is hard to know unless write offs are tracked by payer and by reason each month, and your biller holds that claim detail. Lucid reconciles deposits to the bank and tracks payer mix, so the cash that arrives can be checked against what your biller reports.

faq.q: Should my therapists be W-2 employees or paid on a 1099?
faq.a: It depends on how much control you have over their schedule, methods and patients, and the rules differ by state. Lucid reviews how your therapists are paid from the tax side and tells you where the risk looks high, so you can take it to your attorney. Lucid does not give legal advice.

faq.q: Does Lucid do my billing or chase insurance?
faq.a: No. Lucid works alongside your biller. Lucid handles the books, taxes and CFO reporting, and gives you clear numbers on payer mix and margin per clinic.
